assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (proglucagon processing, incretin action, insulinotropic activity of the truncated peptide) led to incretin therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity of mechanism and breadth of clinical impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (biology, gut and pancreatic actions, translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 7-36 peptide) form a coherent three-person configuration. Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide) and others are credited but would be excluded; the allocation between basic discovery and drug development is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Therapies have been in wide use for years with large randomized outcome trials and independent confirmation; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit dispute around Mojsov versus other groups for the active peptide is unresolved in my recollection and I have not verified it.
Excluding the drug-development contributors (e.g. Knudsen) could be contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a dominant driver of synovial inflammation and that its blockade controls rheumatoid arthritis established anti-cytokine therapy and changed outcomes across rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. This is a clear translational discovery with a bedside-to-bench logic.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the key mechanistic and clinical proof-of-concept work, and the two-person configuration is clean. Contributions of antibody engineers and industry developers of infliximab and etanercept could raise allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of clinical use, multiple independent drug classes and biosimilars confirm the finding; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, if not late.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the contribution as sufficiently basic rather than therapeutic development.
Prior recognition by Lasker and others does not settle Nobel suitability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed by chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality (living drugs), with approved products and strong conceptual originality.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB, first clinical successes), Sadelain (CD28 co-stimulated CARs, preclinical foundations) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified lymphocytes) is a plausible trio, but Eshhar, Kuwana, Finney, Brenner and others hold earlier claims on CAR design and the choice is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Approved products, large clinical experience and expanding indications (autoimmunity) support maturity; solid-tumour efficacy, toxicity and cost remain limitations but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Founding CAR design credit (Eshhar and others) may be omitted by this credited set.
Whether the prize should reward the clinical translation or the original concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, a signalling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing), revealed a fundamental mechanism of proteostasis with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and inflammatory disease.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori separately defined the pathway components and mechanism (Walter: IRE1 and signalling logic; Mori: transcriptional induction and HAC1/XBP1), a natural two-person configuration. Related early contributions by others (e.g. Sidrauski, Ron) exist.
assessment.maturity: Conceptually established for about three decades with extensive independent confirmation; disease-relevant translation is still maturing.
uncertainties: Direct clinical impact is less established than for therapeutic candidates.
Allocation of credit among additional contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune and interferon responses, with broad significance for infection, autoimmune disease (interferonopathies, lupus), cancer immunity and ageing. Originality and mechanistic clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger), Barber and Ishikawa (STING discovery) represent the key steps; Sun and Wu were co-authors on the cGAS work, and others (Vance, Patel and structural biologists) also contributed. A three-person limit forces exclusions that may be contested.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism strongly confirmed and widely used; therapeutic applications (agonists, inhibitors) are still in trials, so clinical validation is early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-term culture of Lgr5-positive adult stem cells as self-organizing organoids created a widely adopted platform for studying tissue renewal, disease modelling, drug testing and personalised medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is clearly decisive (Lgr5 stem cells and organoid conditions); Sato contributed the intestinal and human organoid culture work. Other contributors in organoid biology (Eiraku, Lancaster, Knoblich, Sasai) address a different, pluripotent-derived approach and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Broadly adopted and reproduced, though clinical impact is still emerging and the field is rapidly evolving.
uncertainties: Whether the technology or its therapeutic yield is Nobel-mature.
Relationship to pluripotent organoid work remains unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia into a manageable disease and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, with striking, durable clinical effect.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical translation), Lydon (compound development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are a plausible trio, though Rowley, Nowell and Hungerford, and Witte or Baltimore on ABL, are part of the broader story and may complicate recognition.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of clinical experience with robust confirmation. Recognition is mature, though some may feel earlier chromosomal and oncogene work should have been honoured first.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with earlier prize-recognized oncogene work.
Whether this is seen as drug development rather than discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity, transforming experimental neuroscience and enabling vision restoration trials.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread among Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann (channelrhodopsin), Boyden, Deisseroth (neuronal application), and Miesenboeck (earlier light-gated approaches); a three-person limit is difficult and there is no agreed split.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated, with early clinical translation emerging; scientific impact is clear but attribution is the main obstacle to timing.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation of credit among six named individuals.
Clinical significance remains limited so far.
